paper_design_summary: TreeWriter was evaluated in three non-overlapping samples: a six-person formative online survey, a 12-person comparative lab study, and an eight-person collaborative field deployment lasting two months. In the lab study, students edited a 4,000-word article and wrote an 800-word opinion essay with TreeWriter and with Google Docs + Gemini, with randomly assigned tool/content order; measures were post-task ratings, the Creativity Support Index, NASA-TLX, and qualitative feedback. The formative survey and field deployment collected questionnaire and interview responses; neither assigned comparison conditions, the deployment provided AI editing buttons without the chat writing assistant, and no study scored creativity or diversity on written output.

eligibility.reason: The comparative lab study randomly assigned within-person tool/content order between two generative-AI configurations (p. 14, Section 5.2; p. 27, Appendix D, Table 6), satisfying criterion 1. Its analyzed cohort is 12 people, evidenced by response counts in Figure 9 (p. 17), below 50; the separately randomized total is not reported. The lab outcomes are questionnaire ratings and qualitative feedback, with no creativity or diversity scored on essays or edits (p. 14, Section 5.4; pp. 26-27, Appendix C; pp. 30-32, Appendix G). The formative survey has six participants (pp. 5-6, Sections 3.1-3.2), and the descriptive field deployment has eight participants with two collaborating authors excluded from that count (p. 18, Section 6). Neither has comparison conditions or creativity/diversity scored on written output (pp. 25-26, Appendix B; pp. 32-33, Appendix H), and the samples do not overlap (p. 25, Appendix A). Thus no study meets all core criteria or a context-evidence category; retain the paper only in the screening report.

one_line_finding: In a within-subjects lab study with 12 students, participants rated TreeWriter above Google Docs + Gemini on self-reported idea exploration (q = 0.01), CSI creativity (q = 0.033), and CSI idea tracking (q = 0.033) (p. 30, Appendix G; Figures 8-9, pp. 16-17); no written output was scored.
